post.summary: Create an upload URL for a single-file asset
post.description: For an asset created without `url`, `base64`, or `parts`. Send the file to `uploadUrl` with the returned `method` and `headers`, then call `:completeUpload`. The asset moves to `UPLOADING`. Call again for a new URL while the upload is unfinished. A typed asset uses `:createUploadUrls` instead.

post.summary: Create a download URL for one asset
post.description: Returns a short-lived URL that downloads the bytes of a `READY` asset. Fetch it without credentials. An asset withheld under the content policy returns `403` with code `CONTENT_POLICY`.

post.summary: Create upload URLs for a typed asset's parts
post.description: Returns new upload URLs for the parts of a typed asset, for example when the ones from the create response expired. Only an asset whose upload is unfinished accepts this call.

post.summary: Finish an upload and make the asset ready
post.description: Call once after every upload has finished. Checks that the bytes are stored, reads their type, size, and dimensions, and returns the asset as `READY`. Repeating the call on a `READY` asset is safe and returns it again.

post.summary: Create one download credential for a project's assets
post.description: Returns one short-lived credential that reads every `READY` asset in the API key's project. Build each download URL as `baseUrl + contentPath + "?" + signedQuery`.

webhookUrl.title: Webhookurl

purgeContentOnOperationCompletion.title: Purgecontentonoperationcompletion
purgeContentOnOperationCompletion.description: Purge this operation's outputs and the transient uploads it consumed one hour after it finishes. Omitted, the account's setting applies; true raises it for this operation; false is refused when the account already purges. Uploads in the library are never purged by an operation.

base64Outputs.title: Base64Outputs
base64Outputs.description: When a ?wait=true submission is answered inline, return each output file as base64 in that response rather than by assetId and url. This skips storing the files before the answer and the caller's download after it. Any other submission, and every later read of the operation, names the outputs by assetId and url.

targetFrames.title: Targetframes
targetFrames.description: The views to generate, in output order, returned in `frames`: one posed frame per view. Each target frame requires a `camera` at 1280x720 with pinhole intrinsics. At most 1440 frames. A frame that carries only its camera generates from the prompt and contextFrames alone. Otherwise each frame carries a depth, an imageAsset (the view's known pixels), or both, and may carry a maskAsset (8-bit grayscale, white where the frame's image and depth are known). For each of `depth`, `imageAsset`, `maskAsset`, and `depth.maskAsset`, include that field on every target frame in the request or omit it from all of them. The model keeps the image where the mask is set and generates the rest, takes frames without masks as fully known, conditions on the depth alone for frames without an image, and for frames without depth keeps the image inside the mask and generates the geometry. A `depth.maskAsset` (8-bit grayscale on the depth grid, white where the depth is known) masks the depth separately from the image. With a depth mask, `maskAsset` marks only the image and requires an `imageAsset`. Both masks read as known above half intensity. Frames carry no depth confidenceAsset.

contextFrames.title: Contextframes
contextFrames.description: Posed RGB photographs of the scene, each an image and its camera in the targets' coordinate convention and scale. The generated views use them as visual references for materials, colors, and lighting. Any cameras and any resolution; each image is scaled to cover the output dimensions, then center-cropped onto 1280x720. Frames carry no maskAsset or depth. Together with targetFrames they share the served model's rollout, and a request that overflows it fails.

styleReferenceImageAsset.description: Optional style-reference image whose look (medium, palette, lighting) the generated views match; it supplies no camera or geometry, so the prompt and the frames still set the layout.

enhancePrompt.title: Enhanceprompt
enhancePrompt.description: Expand the prompt into a detailed scene description before generation. Set false to use your wording unchanged.

voxelSize.title: Voxelsize
voxelSize.description: Side length of the cubes used to simplify depth geometry. Uses normalized scene units, not input distance units: the scene is rescaled so the 90th percentile of inverse depth is approximately 1. The recommended range is 0 to 0.4. Omit or set to 0 to keep the original geometry.

voxelGridOrientation.title: Voxelgridorientation
voxelGridOrientation.description: Grid orientation for simplifying depth geometry. 'world' (the default) aligns the grid with the request's world axes so walls aligned with those axes stay flat. 'gauge' aligns the grid with the average camera pose after recentering the scene. Ignored unless voxelSize is set.

returnDepth.title: Returndepth
returnDepth.description: Return the generated frames as posed RGBD: they are reconstructed together so the depth lands in the request's own camera frame and scale, and every entry in `frames` then carries a `depth` buffer. The targetFrames' own depth is not reconstructed or returned, and context photographs get no depth back. Needs 2 to 256 target frames. Limitation: the depth scale is recovered from the camera centers that joined, so targets that share one center (a pure-rotation rig) and nothing else anchoring them come back with a 0.0 or NaN scale and a success status.

frames.title: Frames
frames.description: Generated RGB frames (image + camera), one per target frame in order.

purgeContentOnOperationCompletion.title: Purgecontentonoperationcompletion
purgeContentOnOperationCompletion.description: Purge this operation's outputs and the transient uploads it consumed one hour after it finishes. Omitted, the account's setting applies; true raises it for this operation; false is refused when the account already purges. Uploads in the library are never purged by an operation.

base64Outputs.title: Base64Outputs
base64Outputs.description: When a ?wait=true submission is answered inline, return each output file as base64 in that response rather than by assetId and url. This skips storing the files before the answer and the caller's download after it. Any other submission, and every later read of the operation, names the outputs by assetId and url.

contextFrames.title: Contextframes
contextFrames.description: Posed RGBD context views: each an image, its depth buffer, and its camera, all required. All context cameras must declare the same width and height. Context depth is required and provides geometry references for generation. Undistort fisheye or lens-distorted images before upload, and align depth and camera intrinsics to the resulting pinhole image grid.

targetCameras.title: Targetcameras
targetCameras.description: Pinhole cameras for the views to generate, in output order. Generated frames are returned in `frames`, one per camera. All cameras share one size (width x height): 1280x720, 960x720, 528x704, or 720x1280. Camera intrinsics use a pinhole model; lens-distortion coefficients are not accepted.

prompt.title: Prompt
prompt.description: Optional description of the scene's content and appearance, for example "A quiet stone courtyard at blue hour". Do not use editing instructions such as "add a car to the scene" or camera-trajectory descriptions such as "rotate around the person".

enhancePrompt.title: Enhanceprompt
enhancePrompt.description: Expand the prompt into a scene description before generation. With no prompt, describe the context images. Set false to use your wording unchanged.

returnDepth.title: Returndepth
returnDepth.description: Return the generated frames as posed RGBD in the request's camera frame and scale; every entry in `frames` then carries a `depth` buffer. A request whose cameras all share one center (a pure-rotation rig) is rejected because depth scale requires a camera baseline. For 720x1280 targets, more than 11 context frames, or more than 32 target cameras, depth is reconstructed after generation: context and target cameras must share an aspect ratio, and every target principal point must be within 5% of the image center along each axis, or the request is rejected. A context image anchors that reconstruction only when its principal point is centered. Other requests do not require these additional aspect-ratio and principal-point checks.

frames.title: Frames
frames.description: Generated RGB frames (image + camera), one per target camera in order. Every frame also carries a `depth` buffer when the request set returnDepth.

promptUsed.title: Promptused
promptUsed.description: Final prompt supplied to inference, if any.

CamerasAutoAnchors.title: CamerasAutoAnchors
CamerasAutoAnchors.description:
Find anchor positions automatically, then render from them.

Candidates come from the free space the geometry encloses, and `oriented`
picks which rule judges one valid. The default when a request names no
cameras.

CamerasExteriorSphere.title: CamerasExteriorSphere
CamerasExteriorSphere.description:
Render from a sphere around the splats, looking inward.

For anything whose surface can be seen from outside -- an object, a turntable
capture -- no anchors are needed. Cameras are spread evenly over a sphere
bounding the splats and aimed at its center. Naming an
`orientedBoundingBox` sizes that sphere on the splats inside it, which is
what picks one object out of a larger capture.

anchors.title: Anchors

CamerasManualAnchors.title: CamerasManualAnchors
CamerasManualAnchors.description:
Render from explicitly placed anchor positions.

A cubemap is rendered at each anchor, and more cameras are sampled around
it. Anchors belong in open space, with a clear view of the regions that
matter most.

(right-down-forward, the OpenCV convention). Both the ``coordinateSystem``

depth.description: Linear-depth EXR in world units, aligned to camera, beside a confidence map. Multiple frames carry the calibrated keep-probability ('ultimate'); a single frame carries the backbone's own mask ('model'), the only score one view can support. Unproject the depth with the camera intrinsics to recover camera-space points in Three.js convention.

centroidWorld.title: Centroidworld
centroidWorld.description: Ground-plane pivot formed from the mean finite camera-space point transformed into world space and projected to y=0.

Images2PosedRGBDPerImageResult.title: Images2PosedRGBDPerImageResult
Images2PosedRGBDPerImageResult.description:
Per-image reconstruction output.

Geometry is the depth EXR: unproject it with ``camera`` to recover the
camera-space point cloud. ``camera``'s intrinsics describe the depth grid,
which is whatever grid the backbone reconstructed on, so they are not
necessarily the intrinsics of ``imageAsset``.

webhookUrl.description: Where Atlas POSTs one signed task.succeeded or task.failed event when this operation finishes; retried for 24 hours. Verify the signature with the public keys at /.well-known/webhooks/jwks.json. Cannot be combined with ?wait=true. https on port 443 only, no IP literals. Developer API only.

purgeContentOnOperationCompletion.title: Purgecontentonoperationcompletion
purgeContentOnOperationCompletion.description: Purge this operation's outputs and the transient uploads it consumed one hour after it finishes. Omitted, the account's setting applies; true raises it for this operation; false is refused when the account already purges. Uploads in the library are never purged by an operation.

base64Outputs.title: Base64Outputs
base64Outputs.description: When a ?wait=true submission is answered inline, return each output file as base64 in that response rather than by assetId and url. This skips storing the files before the answer and the caller's download after it. Any other submission, and every later read of the operation, names the outputs by assetId and url.

frames.title: Frames
frames.description: Ordered image inputs (min 1). A frame that carries a camera, a depth buffer or a mask is rejected rather than quietly ignored: none of them reaches the reconstruction.

canonicalizeToFirstFrame.title: Canonicalizetofirstframe
canonicalizeToFirstFrame.description: Place the first camera at the origin facing forward.

targetResolution.title: Targetresolution
targetResolution.description: Return the depth, confidence and camera intrinsics on this (width, height) pixel grid: one of 1280 by 720, 720 by 1280, 960 by 720 or 528 by 704, the grids the depth model serves. The reconstruction is scaled to cover the requested size and center-cropped to it, so the result is exactly the size asked for and never stretched, and the intrinsics are updated with it -- unprojecting the returned depth with the returned camera gives the same geometry either way. A requested aspect that differs from the frames' costs field of view, since the crop is what makes the size exact, and centroidWorld then describes the cropped view. Omit it (or pass null) and a multi-view capture with camera translation comes back on whichever of those four grids is closest in aspect to the frames: smaller frames are scaled up onto it, and other aspects (square or 3:2, for example) are center-cropped onto the closest one, with squares going to 960 by 720. A single image or a capture without camera translation comes back on the reconstruction backend's native grid. Set it when a later step needs a particular grid: atlasGenerate, for example, needs context frames with the same aspect as its target cameras.

refinePoses.title: Refineposes
refinePoses.description: Bundle-adjust the estimated cameras against dense matches before answering. The backbone's poses are good to about half a degree, which is enough to reconstruct from and not enough to refine against: the residual shows up as blur wherever two views disagree. The solve anchors on the depth this task has just produced, so it costs a matcher pass and a solve rather than another reconstruction, and it needs two or more frames. A solve that moves the cameras further than the guards allow is thrown away and the unrefined reconstruction is returned, which is a success rather than an error.

refine.title: Refine
refine.description: Run the refiner after drafting: the free-running loop that places cameras, render-difixes them and trains SSO on the draft until its recipe's step count or wall budget, publishing its level under refinedSplats. Off ends the run at the draft pass, fit at 2,000,000 splats by default or at the one targetSplatCounts entry, and published under draftSplat alone. It runs in a fraction of the time and is billed as a draft.

With refine=false, an explicit list must contain exactly one count, the draft's, returned under draftSplat; omitted, the draft is fit at 2,000,000 splats. With refinement the loop's recipe sets the one level it publishes under refinedSplats, and this list is accepted and ignored.

regionOfInterest.description: Oriented box to focus the reconstruction on, or a list of them for separate areas. Each box should enclose both the geometry of interest and the space it can be viewed from. The rest of the scene is still reconstructed from the frames. Omitted, the task covers the whole capture.

halfExtents.title: Halfextents
halfExtents.description: Half the region's size along each of its own axes. All three must be positive.

Splats2MeshOrientedBoundingBox.title: Splats2MeshOrientedBoundingBox
Splats2MeshOrientedBoundingBox.description: Region to extract, as an oriented box in Three.js coordinates.

webhookUrl.title: Webhookurl
webhookUrl.description: Where Atlas POSTs one signed task.succeeded or task.failed event when this operation finishes; retried for 24 hours. Verify the signature with the public keys at /.well-known/webhooks/jwks.json. Cannot be combined with ?wait=true. https on port 443 only, no IP literals. Developer API only.

purgeContentOnOperationCompletion.title: Purgecontentonoperationcompletion
purgeContentOnOperationCompletion.description: Purge this operation's outputs and the transient uploads it consumed one hour after it finishes. Omitted, the account's setting applies; true raises it for this operation; false is refused when the account already purges. Uploads in the library are never purged by an operation.

cameras.title: Cameras
cameras.description: Cameras the splats are rendered from. The surface is reconstructed from those renders, so geometry no camera sees is not meshed. Name a strategy -- `auto_anchors` (the default) finds viewpoints in the scene's free space, `manual_anchors` takes them from the request, `exterior_sphere` rings the scene from outside for an object or turntable capture -- or pass a list of cameras to render as given, at most 512, sharing one width and height between 64 and 1024 that becomes the render resolution.

advancedOptions.description: Finer control over how the splats are rendered and how the surface is extracted. Omit for the defaults.

orientedBoundingBox.description: Region to extract, as an oriented box in Three.js coordinates. Omit to mesh the whole scene.

targetFaces.title: Targetfaces
targetFaces.description: Decimate the extracted mesh to at most this many faces. A target above the extracted count does nothing. Omit to keep every face.

textureMode.title: Texturemode
textureMode.description: Mesh appearance: 'image_texture' projects rendered views onto a UV atlas, 'vertex_color' bakes per-vertex colors, and 'none' leaves the mesh untextured.

textureSize.title: Texturesize
textureSize.description: Height and width of the texture atlas, in pixels, for `image_texture` mode. One rendered view plus its border has to fit, so this must be at least 2% above the render size in play: the larger render bank under the anchor strategies, `renderHw` under `exterior_sphere`, or the supplied cameras' own size.

colliderBoxes.description: Also fit oriented boxes that enclose the mesh, for collision. The boxes stay upright, turning only about the vertical axis, and come back as a second GLB asset with one node per box. Omit to skip them.

splatAsset.description: The Gaussian splat scene (.spz) to mesh. Inline base64 must carry a `data:` prefix to declare its media type: asset creation otherwise infers the type from the bytes, and the sniffer knows image formats only.

colliderBoxes.description: Collider boxes as a GLB, one node per box sharing one cube, in the same coordinates as `mesh`. Null unless the request set `colliderBoxes`.

anchorPositions.title: Anchorpositions
anchorPositions.description: Anchor positions the cameras were generated from, in Three.js coordinates. Null when no anchors were used: cameras were supplied directly, or `exterior_sphere` was chosen.

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.description: Deprecated runtime diagnostics. Informational only -- keys are not part of the contract and may change.

Splats2MeshResponse.title: Splats2MeshResponse
Splats2MeshResponse.description: Public response projected into the completed Operation.

id.title: Id
id.description: Short operation id used in ``/operations/{operation}`` paths.

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.description: Task information and optional progress details. Use ``metadata.task`` to interpret a generic operation response, and use ``done`` to determine completion.

done.title: Done
done.description: Whether the operation is terminal. When true, a non-null ``error`` indicates failure; otherwise the operation succeeded.

error.description: Failure details when ``done`` is true and the task failed; null while running and after success.

expiresAtSecs.title: Expiresatsecs
expiresAtSecs.description: Task execution deadline as Unix seconds, when one is exposed. This is not an asset URL expiration.

createdAtSecs.title: Createdatsecs
createdAtSecs.description: Unix seconds when the operation was accepted.

response.description: ``Splats2MeshResponse`` result when ``done`` is true and the task succeeded; null while running and after failure.

name.title: Name
name.description:
Full resource name for the operation.

For project operations:
``accounts/{account}/projects/{project}/operations/{operation}``.
Operation paths accept the short ``id``.

Splats2MeshResponseOperation.title: Splats2MeshResponseOperation
Splats2MeshResponseOperation.description: Long-running operation whose successful terminal ``response`` has type ``Splats2MeshResponse``. This is the common Operation envelope with a task-specific response type, not a separate operation resource.

base64.title: Base64
base64.description: Base64-encoded media bytes, with or without a data URL prefix. Decoded size must be less than 10 MiB. A task response carries inline bytes only when it is returned from the submission; the stored operation names the same output by `assetId` and `url`.

url.title: Url
url.description: Public HTTP(S) URL containing the media. On a task response this is a read URL for `assetId` and it expires; mint a fresh one with `assets/{asset}:createReadUrl`.

TaskAsset.title: TaskAsset
TaskAsset.description:
Media named by asset id, inline base64, or public URL.

A task response names each output by id and url together: the url expires,
the id does not. The pair is accepted as input as well, so a response can
be handed straight back to the next task; the id names the media and the
url is ignored. Inline base64 stands alone. A response returns it only
when a task is answered at submission; the stored operation names the
same output by id and url.

role.title: Role
role.description: Declared asset-part role this upload fills.

method.title: Method
method.description: HTTP verb to use for the upload, e.g. PUT.

url.title: Url
url.description: Short-lived upload URL. Send the bytes here without the World Labs API key.

headers.title: Headers
headers.description: Headers the client MUST include on the upload request.

expiresAt.title: Expiresat
expiresAt.description: When this upload grant expires; create a new one after.

UploadGrant.title: UploadGrant
UploadGrant.description: Permission to upload one asset part.

timeoutSecs.title: Timeoutsecs
timeoutSecs.description: Seconds to block waiting for the operation to finish, capped server-side at 30; omit to use the cap. Best-effort: the operation may still be running when this returns.

deliveryId.title: Deliveryid
deliveryId.description: The value sent in the `webhook-id` header; absent while SCHEDULED or PUBLISH_FAILED.

webhookUrl.title: Webhookurl
webhookUrl.description: The accepted webhookUrl; absent once the operation's content was purged, while the delivery record itself stays.

state.title: State
state.description: SCHEDULED until the operation is terminal and handed over; PUBLISH_FAILED when Atlas could not hand the completion to its webhook service (poll the operation instead); then the delivery's own state: PENDING (waiting for the next attempt), IN_FLIGHT, DELIVERED, SUPPRESSED (the receiver answered 410), EXHAUSTED (the 24-hour window closed, or after one attempt when the webhookUrl host resolves to a private address). A cancelled operation sends no event and answers 404.

event.title: Event
event.description: The exact event body sent, once the delivery exists.

attemptCount.title: Attemptcount
attemptCount.description: Sends attempted so far; a claim counts before its outcome.

nextAttemptTime.title: Nextattempttime
nextAttemptTime.description: Scheduled time of the next attempt while PENDING.

purgeTime.title: Purgetime
purgeTime.description: Expires 90 days after the webhook service accepted the delivery.

WebhookDelivery.title: WebhookDelivery
WebhookDelivery.description: The callback record for one operation.

httpStatus.title: Httpstatus
httpStatus.description: The receiver's status, if it answered.

errorCategory.title: Errorcategory
errorCategory.description: Why the attempt did not get a status: a send that failed (timeout, connect_error, tls_error, internal, proxy_rejected:<reason> such as dns_error or private_address), or a close with no send (expired, purged, account_deleted); `publish_failed` while PUBLISH_FAILED.

WebhookDeliveryAttempt.title: WebhookDeliveryAttempt
WebhookDeliveryAttempt.description: The latest send's outcome; never the receiver's body.

attemptCount.title: Attemptcount
attemptCount.description: Sends attempted so far; a claim counts before its outcome.

WebhookDeliverySummary.title: WebhookDeliverySummary
WebhookDeliverySummary.description:
A listed operation's callback at a glance; its webhookDelivery has the
full record.
